text:
sec-oncall: P1 — CI npm auth token found in build cache logs. Token belonged to the CI deployer account and had package publish scope for @redwood/*.
sec-oncall: Immediate actions required for all teams using the repo CI: 1) Revoke the affected token(s). 2) Rotate any npm tokens used by CI runners. 3) Search caches and artifacts for plaintext tokens and remove/rotate. 4) Audit recent package publishes and revert any suspicious packages.
sec-oncall: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ci-token-leak — follow the checklist under "revoke-and-rotate". If you are the owner of a CI pipeline, please ack and start rotation now.
ci-bot: automated alert: anomaly detected in build logs on runner r-ci-14 — potential secret pattern matched: /:_authToken=\w{20,}/ — see pipeline 4321
alice: ack — which repos are in scope? I saw the alert referencing infra/website and sdk/*
sec-oncall: scope = all repos that use shared CI runner pool and cache uploads. Initial findings show token came from infra/website pipeline cache upload step. Treat as org-wide potential exposure until we finish grep sweep.
bob: I'm starting a rotation for the CI deployer token now. ETA ~15m. Will post new token location after it's stored in Vault.
devops: paused cache uploads across the runner pool: disabled step `upload-cache` on all active pipelines. Will notify CI runners team.
eng-manager: any sign of customer data being exposed or package tampering in production apps?
sec-oncall: no evidence of PII exfiltration so far. We have detected a new package publish to @redwood/ui with a bumped minor — investigating. If you maintain packages, check versions since today 09:00 UTC.
qa-lead: starting quick dependency scan and verifying package checksums for prod services.
alice: grep command I'll run for everyone: `git grep -n "_authToken" || grep -R "_authToken" /build/cache || rg "_authToken" --hidden /shared/cache`
sec-oncall: good. Also run this to list any npm tokens in Vault (for owners): `vault list secret/ci/npm-tokens` then `vault read secret/ci/npm-tokens/<id>` to identify owners. Rotate using our token rotation script: `/scripts/rotate-npm-token.sh <token-id>`
deploy-bot: token revoke request accepted for token id=tok-4587 by bob
deploy-bot: token status: revoked
bob: token revoked and new token stored in Vault at secret/ci/npm-tokens/tok-8590. I removed write scope from the fallback token as a safety measure.
devops: CI caches disabled, cache scrub job queued: `scripts/scrub-ci-cache --paths /shared/cache --pattern "*_authToken*"` — running now.
eng-manager: please post a short summary for execs when we have containment timeline. Include impact and mitigations.
sec-oncall: will prepare a one-pager. For now: containment in progress, token revoked, caches scrubbed, publishing blocked until audit complete. If you find any additional leaks, ping me and post: @sec-oncall @devops.
qa-lead: found one artifact with embedded token in build-2026. Replaced artifact and invalidated release candidate.
alice: thanks — doing a final grep pass across all repos and will share the list in this thread.
sec-oncall: thanks everyone. Treat this as high priority. I'll update timeline in 30m. :shield:
